card.title: Ecological Imbalances — Pollution and Climate Change

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Human activities cause ecological imbalances: the enhanced greenhouse effect (CO2, CH4, CFCs) drives climate change; CFCs deplete the ozone layer, increasing UV radiation; SO2 and NOx cause acid rain (pH < 5.6); and biological invasions (e.g., water hyacinth in Nepal) threaten native biodiversity. These imbalances cause biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, and health problems.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Greenhouse effect: GHG (CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs) + IR radiation → warming
Ozone depletion: CFC → Cl atom → O3 → O2 (chain reaction)
Acid rain: SO2 + H2O → H2SO4; NOx + H2O → HNO3 (pH < 5.6)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: The greenhouse effect is a NATURAL phenomenon (essential for life); the "enhanced" greenhouse effect (due to human emissions) causes climate change.  ·  Ozone layer depletion (stratospheric O3 destroyed by CFCs) is different from the greenhouse effect (tropospheric gases trapping heat).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects clear explanations of the greenhouse effect, ozone depletion, acid rain, and biological invasion.  ·  The natural vs enhanced greenhouse effect distinction is a common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Greenhouse effect: CO2 + CH4 + CFCs trap infrared radiation → warming.  ·  Ozone depletion: CFCs (from refrigerators, aerosols) release Cl atoms → destroy O3 → increased UV → skin cancer.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Acid rain is caused by SO2 and NOx (industry, vehicles), NOT by CO2 alone.  ·  Biological invasion involves NON-NATIVE species; it is different from natural colonisation.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Explain greenhouse effect  ·  Explain ozone depletion

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Greenhouse = GHGs + IR → warming (natural + enhanced).  ·  Ozone = CFCs → Cl → O3 destruction → UV → cancer.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Explain the greenhouse effect and its causes.  ·  Describe the effects of climate change on ecosystems.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Explain the greenhouse effect and climate change.  ·  Explain ozone layer depletion (CFCs, UV).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Greenhouse effect (natural + enhanced)  ·  Climate change  ·  Ozone layer depletion (CFCs)  ·  Acid rain (SO2, NOx)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Greenhouse effect: GHGs trap heat → climate change (natural + enhanced).  ·  Ozone depletion: CFCs destroy stratospheric O3 → increased UV → skin cancer.  ·  Acid rain: SO2 + NOx → H2SO4, HNO3 → pH < 5.6 → damage to forests, water, buildings.  ·  Biological invasion: non-native species outcompete natives → biodiversity loss.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Atmospheric CO2 has risen from ~280 ppm (pre-industrial) to ~420 ppm (2023).  ·  Global average temperature has risen ~1.1°C since pre-industrial times.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain ozone layer depletion and its consequences.  ·  Describe acid rain (causes, effects, control).  ·  Explain biological invasion with a Nepali example.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: List control measures for ecological imbalances.  ·  Explain Nepal's vulnerability to climate change.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Acid rain: SO2 (coal plants) + NOx (vehicles) → H2SO4, HNO3 in rain → acidic rain → forest damage, lake acidification.  ·  Biological invasion: water hyacinth in Phewa Lake, Pokhara → smothered native fish and plants → oxygen depletion.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The main cause of ozone layer depletion is: → B  ·  Acid rain has a pH of: → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Ecological imbalances: human-induced disruptions of natural ecosystems.  ·  Greenhouse effect and climate change: greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs) trap heat → global warming; effects: melting ice, rising sea levels, extreme weather, habitat loss.  ·  Ozone layer depletion: CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) destroy stratospheric ozone (O3) → increased UV radiation → skin cancer, cataracts, crop damage.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nepal vulnerability  ·  In an ecosystem one can observe the transfer or flow of energy from one trophic level to other trophic level by the process of eating and being eaten.  ·  It forms a linear chain called food chain.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: There are basically three types of food chain in nature: 1.  ·  Grazing food chain: The food chain that starts from the green plants and ends to carnivores (top consumer) by passing though herbivores.  ·  Detritus food chain: The organic wastes and dead matter derived from grazing food chain are called as detritus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Key concept 1 for 05 ecological imbalances greenhouse effects and climate change depletion of ozone layer acid rain and biological invasion.  ·  Biological invasion: non-native species → outcompete natives → biodiversity loss  ·  Causes: deforestation, industry, urbanisation, overpopulation, pollution.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Effects: biodiversity loss, ecosystem degradation, climate change, health problems.  ·  Control: reduce emissions, plant trees, sustainable agriculture, international agreements.  ·  Climate change affects ecosystems at all scales (local to global).
